matched: Development of logistic regression (LR) framework to probabilistically predict effluent ammonium nitrogen (NH4-Neff) and quantify water reuse potential in outdoor MPBR treating municipal wastewater
Framework demonstrated effective prediction and control based on 1.5 years of pilot-scale operational data
Local sensitivity analysis showed photosynthetic activity (DO, DOmax) and ambient temperature exerted strongest influence on predicted NH4-Neff
Relevance of aeration flow rate (Fair) increased markedly during high-ammonium episodes
Relying solely on HRT and SRT is insufficient for maintaining optimal long-term performance under fluctuating outdoor conditions
In-silico simulation of advanced control strategy simultaneously optimising SRT, HRT, NLR, and Fair projected 12-50% reduction in NH4-Neff and 32-38% reduction in aeration demand
Integration of LR framework with SCADA system across 5 data-acquisition scenarios (A-E) balancing online measurements and virtual sensors
LR framework presents a promising, highly interpretable alternative to complex mechanistic control models and black-box machine learning algorithms

Methodology validated on pilot-scale data and computational simulations; broad applicability requires validation across full-scale reactor designs, varying wastewater characteristics, and climatic conditions
